1.note: Zechariah is using the word translated as **returned** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

The point of this comparison is that just as a man who is roused from his sleep is awakened suddenly, so the angel is rousing Zechariah to pay attention. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as when a man is suddenly awakened from sleep]

The expression **is roused from his sleep** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [who someone wakes from sleep]

2.note: The angel is using the possessive form to describe a **bowl** that belongs to the lampstand. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the bowl on top of it]

2.q: וְ⁠שִׁבְעָ֤ה נֵרֹתֶ֨י⁠הָ֙ עָלֶ֔י⁠הָ שִׁבְעָ֤ה וְ⁠שִׁבְעָה֙ מֽוּצָק֔וֹת
2.note: Translate this number according to the conventions of your own language and culture. Alternate translation: [and seven lamps on it, fourteen tubes]

Zechariah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [and look]

3.note: The pronoun **it** refers to the bowl. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [are beside the bowl]

4.note: The term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

5.note: The angel is using the question form to express that Zechariah should already know what the items mean. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You should know what these are.]
The pronoun **these** refers to the lampstand and the two olive trees. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the lampstand and olive trees are]

The terms **answered and said** together introduce a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent both terms explicitly.

6.note: The angel is using the possessive form to describe a **word** that comes from Yahweh. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the word from Yahweh]

6.q: לֹ֤א בְ⁠חַ֨יִל֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א בְ⁠כֹ֔חַ כִּ֣י אִם־בְּ⁠רוּחִ֔⁠י
6.note: The angel is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [You will not accomplish this by your own might or power, but my Spirit will accomplish it]

6.q: אֵלַ⁠י֙ לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר זֶ֚ה דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א
6.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [to me that this is the message from Yahweh to Zerubbabel: “Not]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **might** and **power,** you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [Not by strength and not by force]

The terms **might** and **power** mean similar things. The angel is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Not by your own strength]

7.note: The angel is speaking to the great mountain that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about how the obstacles before Zerubbabel will be removed. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if the angel were speaking directly to the people about the mountain. Alternate translation: [Now about this great mountain in front of Zerubbabel, it will become a plain.]

Here the angel is speaking as if the great mountain were a person standing in the way. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [What are you, great obstacle, before Zerubbabel? You will no longer block him!]

The angel is using the question form to emphasize that the mountain obstacle will be removed. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You are nothing, great mountain, before Zerubbabel]
The pronoun **he** refers to Zerubbabel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Zerubbabel will bring out]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [while people call out blessings on it]

The angel is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling, joy. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. If not, you could say what the angel was feeling, or you could say what caused him to feel joyful. Alternate translation: [What joy! Let joy be upon it!]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **grace,** you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Blessed! Blessed!]

Zechariah is repeating the word **Grace** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [May God greatly bless it]

The pronoun **it** refers to the top stone or the temple. The angel is using the top stone to represent the completed temple. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to the top stone] or [to the temple]

8.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 4:6. Alternate translation: [the word from Yahweh]
The term “saying” introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

9.q: יְדֵ֣י זְרֻבָּבֶ֗ל יִסְּד֛וּ הַ⁠בַּ֥יִת הַ⁠זֶּ֖ה וְ⁠יָדָ֣י⁠ו תְּבַצַּ֑עְנָה
9.note: Here, **hands** represents the work and effort of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Zerubbabel’s work has founded this house, and his work will complete it.]
The pronoun **you** refers to Zerubbabel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And you, Zerubbabel, will know]

The pronoun **me** could refer to: (1) the angel speaking to Zechariah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [has sent his angelic messenger to you] or (2) to Zechariah. Alternate translation: [has sent me, Zechariah, to you]
The word **you** is plural here because Yahweh is addressing the people, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

10.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the people. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the people will be glad and will see]

Yahweh is speaking of the eyes as if they were living things that could roam. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they look throughout all the earth]

10.q: כִּ֣י מִ֣י בַז֮ לְ⁠י֣וֹם קְטַנּוֹת֒ וְ⁠שָׂמְח֗וּ
10.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [Indeed, who would despise the day of small beginnings? It is certain that people will rejoice]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **day** that is characterized by small things. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the day when small things happen]

Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that no one should despise small beginnings. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [no one should despise the day of small things!]

A **stone of tin** refers to a metal or stone weight tied to a line and hung down from the top of a wall to make sure it is perfectly straight up and down. The common term for this is “plumb line,” as in the UST. If your readers would not be familiar with what a plumb line is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a measuring string] or [a device that proves that the building was constructed properly]
The pronoun **These** refers to the seven lamps. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [These seven lamps are]

Here, **eyes** represents the awareness and watchfulness of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh’s watchfulness]

11.note: The terms **answered and said** together introduce a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent both terms explicitly.

12.note: If your language would not represent a number in a form such as “second,” you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [again]
The pronoun **them** refers to the two olive branches. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [that are emptying the gold from upon the two branches]

Here Zechariah is speaking as if the olive oil were gold because of its preciousness and golden color. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [emptying the olive oil from upon them]

13.note: The pronoun **he** refers to the angel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the angel said to me]

The angel is using the question form to express that Zechariah should already know what the items mean. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. See how you translated the similar expression in 4:5. Alternate translation: [You should know what these are.]

14.note: The angel is using the possessive form to describe a **Lord** who rules all the earth. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the Lord who rules all the earth]

The angel is using **sons of the fresh oil** as a common expression of the culture to mean the people who have been anointed to serve. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [are the two servants who were anointed]
